prompt:
Return only one JSON object with exactly the keys name, phone, email, company, country. Each value is a string or JSON null. Do not output Markdown, commentary, or questions.

1. Locate the single contact block inside the note. Accept label variants for the five fields, in any order, with colon, equals or tab separators. Use only values in that block. Never draw values from surrounding notes, signatures, domains or legal suffixes. Trim each value and collapse whitespace runs to a single space. Treat absent values, empty values and these case-insensitive placeholders as missing: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD. Missing fields output null, except for the country fallback below.

2. Assign across the block before formatting. A value with @ goes to email, regardless of label. A value goes to phone if, after stripping a leading tel: and a trailing extension, it has at least seven digits and consists only of digits, spaces and + - ( ) . /. Extension forms are ext. 12, ext 12, x12, #12 and extension 12, with the digits varying. Use the country line alone for explicit country. Take name and company from their labelled lines, swapping them if the name-labelled value ends in a listed legal suffix and the company-labelled value does not.

3. Resolve country and phone. Convert a present country to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 from an English, Swedish or German name, alpha-2 or alpha-3 code, or common alias, ignoring case. UK and Great Britain map to GB, Holland to NL, USA and U.S.A. to US, Türkiye to TR, and Czech Republic to CZ.
- International phone: on the extension-free, tel:-free number, ignore an opening parenthesis and check for an initial + or 00. Convert a leading 00 to +, delete (0), and remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses. Keep the calling code as written, even if it disagrees with the explicit country. If the country line is missing, empty or a placeholder, fill country only when the calling code identifies exactly one country; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave it null. This fallback overrides missingness only for country.
- National phone: remove formatting and one initial trunk 0, then prefix + and the calling code of the normalised country. If there is no country, output null for the national phone.
- Missing phone: output null. A non-null phone is E.164: + followed only by calling-code and national-significant-number digits.

4. Format name, company and email. For name, split at the first comma if present and move the part after it before the part before it. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx and Prof, with or without a dot, ignoring case. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated name part. Keep Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate. Strings are compared after NFC normalisation.
For company, strip one trailing legal suffix and an optional comma before it. Match the suffix case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated company word.
For email, remove the mailto: prefix and surrounding angle brackets, then lowercase the whole address.

Emit all five keys, using JSON null, not a quoted placeholder, for missing results.
